sentences.text: This ancient shark possessed seven fins, teeth of varying shapes, and relatively long, deep lower jaws.
Fossil evidence suggests the animal was a relatively large shark, likely exceeding one meter in length when fully grown.
The genus was discovered in Carboniferous terrains in Scotland and the Paraná Basin in Brazil, inhabiting ancient fresh water systems.
Findings from the Puertollano Basin in Spain suggest that the animal also lived in zones of marine influence, such as brackish waters.
There are 11 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus in the Paleobiology Database.
Unlike modern sharks, this species inhabited fresh water lagoons and likely hunted small fish.
It is possible that the animal preyed on its smaller relatives.
The genus was described by Agassiz in 1837.
The type species of the genus is Sphenacanthus serrulatus.
It belongs to the family Sphenacanthidae.
The animal is classified within the order Ctenacanthiformes.
It is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
Sphenacanthus belongs to the subclass Elasmobranchii.
The animal is within the kingdom Animalia.
It belongs to the phylum Chordata.
The species lived approximately 359 million years ago and is considered one of the earliest members of the elasmobranch lineage leading to modern sharks.
